question: Should OpenClaw sponsor consent-bound, core-managed workspace-file creation and durable per-file provenance as part of the experimental Claws lifecycle?
rationale: The patch is a coherent feature slice with no established current-main behavior to repair; acceptance chooses whether this persistent lifecycle belongs in core and whether the dependent stack should proceed.

options.title: Sponsor the lifecycle slice
options.body: Accept managed, create-only workspace files and per-file provenance as an experimental Claws core contract, subject to the exact-head merge gates.

options.title: Keep Claws planning-only
options.body: Decline workspace mutation in core for now and leave the stack open only if a narrower owner-approved direction is proposed.

options.title: Move the capability outside core
options.body: Require an external plugin or ClawHub implementation if maintainers do not want this workspace ownership model in the core lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the lifecycle slice
recommendation.body: Accept managed, create-only workspace files and per-file provenance as an experimental Claws core contract, subject to the exact-head merge gates.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment identifies the key workspace identity and fs-safe invariants, making them the strongest evidenced technical routing candidate in the supplied discussion.
